title: Structural Neuroimaging: X-ray CT, MRI, & Diffusion Tensor Imaging (DTI)
description: Understand anatomical imaging: CT density, MRI magnetic fields and T1/T2 relaxation, and DTI white matter tractography.

slides.title: Imaging the Static Anatomy of the Living Brain 📷
slides.content:
# Peer Through the Skull

Before modern neuroimaging, anatomists could only examine brain structure post-mortem. Today, non-invasive structural techniques allow us to map neural tissue at millimeter and sub-millimeter resolution in living individuals.

* **Computerized Tomography (CT)**: Slices of X-ray beams rotate around the head. Tissues absorb X-rays based on density (bone is dense/white; air/fluid is black; brain parenchyma is gray). Excellent for rapid emergency detection of skull fractures, acute intracranial hemorrhages, and large strokes.

slides.title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI): Nuclear Physics at Work 🧲
slides.content:
## The Physics of MRI

1. **The Magnetic Field ($B_0$)**: The patient lies within a massive superconducting magnet (typically 1.5 to 3 Tesla, 60,000 times Earth's magnetic field!). The magnetic field aligns the spin axes of billions of **hydrogen protons** (abundant in water and fat).
2. **Radiofrequency (RF) Pulse**: An RF pulse tuned to the protons' resonant frequency tilts their net magnetization vector into the transverse plane.
3. **Relaxation & Signal Detection**: When the RF pulse turns off, protons relax back to alignment with $B_0$, emitting tiny radiofrequency signals detected by receiver coils.

### Contrasts:
* **T1-Weighted**: Fat is bright, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is dark. Provides superb gray-matter / white-matter anatomical contrast.
* **T2-Weighted**: Fluid/CSF is bright, white matter is dark. Highly sensitive to edema, tumors, and multiple sclerosis plaques.

quizData.question: Which fundamental atomic nucleus is targeted and aligned by clinical MRI scanners due to its abundance in biological tissue?
quizData.explanation: MRI detects the magnetic resonance of hydrogen nuclei (single protons), which are ubiquitous in biological water and lipid molecules.

slides.title: Diffusion Tensor Imaging (DTI): Mapping White Matter Highways 🛣️
slides.content:
## Visualizing the Brain's Wiring

While conventional MRI shows tissue volume, **Diffusion Tensor Imaging (DTI)** maps the directional orientation of white matter axon bundles:

* **Isotropic Diffusion**: In open fluid (like ventricles), water molecules diffuse randomly in all directions like a sphere.
* **Anisotropic Diffusion**: Inside myelinated axons, water molecules are restricted by hydrophobic myelin walls and diffuse primarily *parallel* to the axonal fiber tract like water in a straw.
* **Fractional Anisotropy (FA) & Tractography**: By measuring anisotropic diffusion along multiple gradient directions, mathematical algorithms reconstruct stunning 3D color-coded maps of major white matter tracts (e.g., Corpus Callosum, Arcuate Fasciculus, Corticospinal Tract).

quizData.question: Diffusion Tensor Imaging (DTI) maps white matter axonal tracts by measuring which physical phenomenon?

options.text: Anisotropic directional diffusion of water molecules along myelin sheaths
X-ray photon attenuation by calcium in the skull
Radioactive decay of fluorine isotopes in the bloodstream
The speed of acoustic vibrations in the cochlea

quizData.explanation: DTI exploits the anisotropic (directionally constrained) diffusion of water along axon bundles to model structural brain connectivity.
